# Exact strings the email check may ignore, one per line — vendor license
# banners that surface inside built client assets, and URL userinfo that only
# LOOKS like an address. Placeholders (@example.com, @example.org, @x.com) are
# always allowed and do not belong here.
TAP_TOKEN@github.com
TOKEN@github.com
# The SSH userinfo every GitHub clone URL carries — `git@github.com:owner/repo.git`.
# It is nobody's address: `git` is the fixed account name GitHub's SSH endpoint
# answers to, and the issue inventory has to recognise that spelling of a remote
# to know which repositories it may ask `gh` about at all.
git@github.com
# URL userinfo in the fixture that proves the webhook masker strips credentials
# (`https://admin:hunter2@internal.example.com/x`). `internal.example.com` is a
# subdomain of an RFC 2606 reserved name, so it is documentation by definition —
# but the always-allowed placeholder list matches `@example.com` exactly, not its
# subdomains, and widening that rule to please one fixture is the kind of
# loosening this gate exists to refuse.
hunter2@internal.example.com
# A real WSL1 kernel banner, verbatim, in the fixture that proves platform.ts
# tells WSL1 from WSL2 — `Linux version 4.4.0-19041-Microsoft (Microsoft@…)`.
# It is a build-host string that happens to match the email shape; changing the
# fixture to please the scanner would make the test stop testing the thing.
Microsoft@Microsoft.com
